claim.quote: We report the final result of the CUORICINO experiment. Operated between 2003 and 2008, with a total exposure of 19.75 kg·y of 130 Te, CUORICINO was able to set a lower bound on the 130 Te 0νββ half-life of 2.8 × 10^24 years at 90% C.L.

date.note: arXiv v1 date; published Astroparticle Physics 34 (2011) 822.

key_value_text.quote: The corresponding upper bound on the neutrino Majorana mass is in the range 300–710 meV, depending on the adopted nuclear matrix element evaluation.

name: 130Te Neutrinoless Double-Beta Decay with CUORICINO

significance.quote: a lower bound on the 130 Te 0νββ half-life of 2.8 × 10^24 years at 90% C.L.

summary.plain: CUORICINO's final result: no neutrinoless double beta decay in tellurium-130. After 19.75 kilogram-years, the half-life must exceed 2.8 x 10^24 years, which limits the Majorana neutrino mass to 300-710 milli-electronvolts depending on the nuclear model.
summary.technical: Final CUORICINO analysis including systematic uncertainties: T1/2(0vbb, 130Te) > 2.8e24 yr at 90 % C.L. with 19.75 kg y of 130Te; <m_ee> bound 300-710 meV depending on the nuclear matrix element.

title: 130Te Neutrinoless Double-Beta Decay with CUORICINO
why_it_matters: The best 130Te result before CUORE; its detector techniques and the lessons about pulse-shape spread led to CUORE-0 and CUORE.
